Create optimizer and objective objects

Source: R/constructors.R
constructors.Rd

The function optimizer() creates an Optimizer object and is equivalent to Optimizer$new().

The function objective() creates an Objective object and is equivalent to Objective$new().

Usage

optimizer(which, ...)

objective(f, target = NULL, npar, ...)

Arguments

which

[character(1)]
Either:

  • one of optimizer_dictionary$keys (the package of the optimizer must be installed)

  • or "custom", in which case $definition() must be used to define the optimizer details.

...

For optimizer(), named arguments to pass to the optimizer algorithm. Additionally, .verbose = FALSE can be set to suppress the status message for which = "custom".

For objective(), optionally additional function arguments that are fixed during the optimization.

f

[function]
A function to be optimized.

target

[character()]
The argument name(s) to optimize.

If NULL (default), the first function argument is selected.

npar

[integer()]
The length of each target argument.

Value

For optimizer(): An Optimizer object.

For objective(): An Objective object.

Examples

### the Rosenbrock function
rosenbrock <- function(x) 100 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)^2 + (1 - x[1])^2

### minimize with 'stats::nlm'
nlm <- optimizer("stats::nlm", iterlim = 200)
nlm$minimize(rosenbrock, initial = c(-1.2, 1))
#> $value
#> [1] 3.973765e-12
#> 
#> $parameter
#> [1] 0.999998 0.999996
#> 
#> $seconds
#> [1] 0.01898527
#> 
#> $initial
#> [1] -1.2  1.0
#> 
#> $error
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $gradient
#> [1] -6.539235e-07  3.335976e-07
#> 
#> $code
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 23
#> 

### evaluate the objective
rosenbrock_objective <- objective(rosenbrock, npar = 2)
rosenbrock_objective$evaluate(c(1, 1))
#> [1] 0
